extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining effective filing dates and applying pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)-(g)/(e) prior-art grounds, including when to use specific form paragraphs for Office actions and how international/provisional/continuation benefit claims affect prior-art dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective filing date for continuation/divisional (35 U.S.C. 120/365(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is a continuation or divisional of one or more earlier U.S. applications or international applications and the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 120 or 365(c) are satisfied, the effective filing date of the claimed invention is the same as the earliest filing date in the line of continuation or divisional applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires satisfaction of the statutory benefit/priority requirements (35 U.S.C. 120/365(c)). See related MPEP sections for determination in PCT national-stage continuations (e.g., §§211.01(c), 1895).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective filing date for continuation-in-part (CIP)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is a continuation-in-part of an earlier U.S. application or international application, any claims in the new application not supported by the specification and claims of the parent application have an effective filing date equal to the actual filing date of the new application; any claims fully supported under 35 U.S.C. 112 by the earlier parent application have the effective filing date of that earlier parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish per-claim support: unsupported/new matter -> new filing date; fully supported claims -> benefit of earlier parent's date under 35 U.S.C.112. Verify written-description support in parent and any intermediate applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective filing date when claiming provisional benefit (35 U.S.C. 119(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application properly claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) to a provisional application, the effective filing date of the claimed invention is the filing date of the provisional application for any claims which are fully supported under the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112 by the provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least one claim in the reference seeking provisional benefit must be supported by the provisional's written description in compliance with pre-AIA 35 U.S.C.112 first paragraph (see Dynamic Drinkware; Amgen v. Sanofi).

rubrics_metrics.name: National-stage applications: actual U.S. filing date equals international filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications that entered the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, the actual U.S. filing date of the application is the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 35 U.S.C. 363 and MPEP §1893.03(b) for national-stage effective filing date determinations and interactions with continuation/divisional/CIP analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) statutory bar (one-year rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A publication or issue date of a reference that is more than one year prior to the effective filing date of the claimed invention qualifies as prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b), resulting in a statutory bar to obtaining a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If public use or sale activity occurred more than one year prior to effective filing, reject under 102(b) (statutory bar) rather than 102(a). Mere public knowledge (without public use/sale/printed publication) does not warrant 102(b) but may provide grounds for 102(a). See MPEP §2139.01 and case law (Ex parte Olah) for business-day extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekend/holiday/filing-day extension for 102(b) (Ex parte Olah rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the last day of the one-year period (dated from the date of publication) falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday, the publication is not a statutory bar under pre-AIA 102(b) if the application is filed on the next succeeding business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to 37 C.F.R. 1.6(a)(2) and 1.10 (e.g., Priority Mail Express provisions) do not affect applicant’s concurrent right to defer filing to the next business day when the last day falls on a non-business day. See Ex parte Olah, 131 USPQ 41 (Bd. App. 1960).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishing public use/sale (102(b)) from mere public knowledge (102(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of public use or sale activity more than one year prior to the effective filing date requires rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b); mere knowledge of the invention by the public does not warrant 102(b) but may warrant rejection under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully evaluate the nature of the disclosure: printed publication/public use/on sale -> 102(b) if >1 year; other public disclosures within the year -> 102(a). See MPEP §§2132 and 2133.03(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior-art date rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) allows the use of certain international application publications, U.S. patent application publications, and certain U.S. patents as prior art as of their respective U.S. filing dates, and may use an international filing date as the prior-art date if the international filing date was on or after November 29, 2000, the international application designated the United States, and it was published by WIPO under PCT Article 21(2) in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References based on international applications filed prior to Nov. 29, 2000 are subject to the pre-AIPA version of 102(e). See MPEP §2136 for detailed examination guidelines. Determine whether the reference’s prior-art date is the international filing date or an earlier U.S. filing date for which priority/benefit is properly claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive entity requirement for applying 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply a reference under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), the inventive entity of the application must be different from that of the reference; with joint inventors, only one joint inventor needs to be different for entities to be considered different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if there are some common joint inventors between the application and the reference, 102(e) may still be applicable if at least one inventive entity differs. Assess inventive-entity overlap carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIPA (pre-November 29, 2000) 35 U.S.C. 102(e) treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: For patents or references resulting from international applications filed before Nov. 29, 2000, pre-AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) (as in force on Nov. 28, 2000) controls; the prior-art date is the earliest of the date of compliance with 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1),(2),(4) or the filing date of the later-filed U.S. continuing application that claimed the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications of international applications filed before Nov. 29, 2000 do not have a pre-AIPA 102(e) date but may be prior art under 102(a)/(b) as of their publication date. Use form paragraph 7.12.01.fti where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: International publications filed before Nov. 29, 2000 are not 102(e) reach-back
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications published by WIPO that were filed before Nov. 29, 2000 (or did not designate the U.S. or were not published in English under PCT Article 21(2)) may not be used to 'reach back' as prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), though they are available as prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of their publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of the Nov. 29, 2000 conditions are unmet, apply 102(a)/(b) as appropriate using publication date. See form paragraphs 7.08.fti and 7.09.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider 102(a) even when 102(e) applies
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a reference qualifies as prior art under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), the examiner should still consider pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) because (1) PCT Article 21(2) publication may be the earliest prior-art date under 102(a), and (2) references applied under 102(e)/(f)/(g) in a 103(a) rejection may be disqualified under 103(c) if the reference and the application were commonly owned or subject to an obligation of common assignment at the time the invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check publication dates and ownership/assignment status. Use 102(a) if it yields an earlier prior-art date or avoids disqualification issues under 103(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) applicability criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: For pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) to apply, the reference must have a publication date earlier than the effective filing date of the application under examination and must not be the inventor's (or at least one joint inventor's) own work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claimed invention was the subject of activity by an entity other than the inventor (e.g., sale, manufacture, or disclosure by at least one joint inventor to another), both 102(a) and 102(b) may be applicable depending on timing. Do not make a 102(a) rejection if applicant made the invention and only disclosed it to others within the one-year grace period prior to filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to apply 102(a) versus 102(b) based on timing of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If evidence only points to public knowledge within the year prior to the effective filing date, pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) applies; if public use/sale/printed publication occurred more than one year prior, pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the nature and timing of the disclosure. Protect applicant grace rights where applicant made the invention and disclosure was within one-year grace period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.06 — notice re prior art available under both pre-AIA and AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this notice in all Office Actions when a prior art rejection is made in an application with actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013 that claims priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph should be used only once in an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.07.fti — Statement of Statutory Basis, pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotation of the appropriate paragraphs of pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 that form the basis for rejections under this section in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute need not be re-cited in all Office actions — required in first actions on the merits and final rejections. Use only once per Office action; for certain applications (filed on/after Mar.16,2013 with earlier priority) precede with form paragraph 7.06. If statute is not being recited in an action on the merits, use form paragraph 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs 7.08.fti–7.11.fti — Pre-AIA 102(a)–(d) specific paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs to state the statutory language for: 7.08.fti (102(a) activity by another), 7.09.fti (102(b) activity more than one year prior), 7.10.fti (102(c) abandonment), and 7.11.fti (102(d) foreign patenting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These form paragraphs must be preceded by 7.07.fti. They may be combined or preceded by others as noted in the Examiner Notes for each paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.12.fti — Pre-AIA 102(e) (AIPA/2002 amendments) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph for pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejections, including the statute text and extensive Examiner Notes specifying when the paragraph should be used (types of references, PCT conditions, benefit/priority claim considerations, provisional support requirements, and non-application of foreign priority claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes include: (1) use only for U.S. patents/pubs filed under 111(a), or PCT-derived refs with international filing date on/after Nov.29,2000, or designating US design patents; (2) consider benefit claims under 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), 386(c) only if subject matter is appropriately supported in earlier-filed disclosures; (3) provisional benefit requires at least one claim in the reference be supported by the provisional in compliance with pre-AIA 112 first paragraph; (4) if PCT publication not in English or did not designate US, may not be applied under 102(e) but may under 102(a)/(b); (5) various additional cautions and precedence rules. Must be preceded by 7.07.fti and may be preceded by 7.08–7.11.fti as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.12.01.fti — Pre-AIPA 102(e) for refs from PCT filed prior to Nov.29,2000
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph for references that are U.S. patents issued directly or indirectly from international applications with international filing dates prior to November 29, 2000; uses pre-AIPA 102(e) rules to determine prior-art date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) use only for U.S. patents issued from national stage/continuations of PCT filings pre-Nov.29,2000; (2) prior-art date may be date of compliance with 371(c)(1),(2),(4) if national stage; (3) if issued from continuing application claiming benefit under 120/121/365(c), prior-art date may be actual U.S. filing date of continuing app; (4) consider benefit claims to earlier-filed U.S. provisionals/nonprovisionals only if subject matter is supported; (5) provisional benefit requires 112 support. Must be preceded by 7.07.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.13.fti — Pre-AIA 102(f) (applicant not the inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph stating pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) that the applicant did not himself invent the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be preceded by 7.07.fti and may be preceded by other relevant paragraphs 7.08–7.12.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.14.fti — Pre-AIA 102(g) (priority of invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph stating pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) concerning priority of invention and the factors to be considered (conception, reduction to practice, diligence, abandonment/suppression/concealment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.07.fti and may be accompanied by 7.08–7.13.fti as appropriate. Use in interference/priority determinations per statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.15.fti — Rejection format for pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a),(b),(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Template rejection: 'Claim(s) [1] is/are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 [2] as being [3] by [4].' with instructions for inserting appropriate paragraph letters, characterization (clearly anticipated/anticipated), and identification of prior art relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.07.fti (and possibly 7.08–7.14.fti or 7.103); if 102(e) also applied use accompanying specific 7.15.01–7.15.03 paragraphs; for certain applications (filed on/after Mar.16,2013 with earlier priority) precede with 7.06. Follow bracket guidance for correct insertion and explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.15.01.fti — Provisional rejection under 102(e) for copending application with common assignee/applicant/joint inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional rejection when a copending application with an earlier filing date (and common assignee/applicant/at least one common joint inventor) discloses the claimed invention; based upon presumption of future publication/patenting of the copending application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for copending apps not yet published under 122. May be overcome by showing under 37 C.F.R. 1.132 that invention disclosed in the copending app was derived from applicant (not 'by another') or by 37 C.F.R. 1.131(a) if not same invention. Cannot be overcome by terminal disclaimer. Consider nonstatutory double patenting and require claim amendment/cancellation as appropriate; use relevant double-patenting paragraphs (8.30–8.39) where needed. For apps with filing dates on/after Mar.16,2013 claiming priority to pre-Mar.16,2013, precede with 7.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.15.02.fti — Rejection under 102(e) where reference has common assignee/applicant/joint inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection that claims are anticipated under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) by a reference that has a common assignee, applicant, or at least one common joint inventor; based on earlier effective U.S. filing date of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) use only when reference is a U.S. patent or publication with earlier effective filing date and has common assignee/applicant/joint inventor; (2) apply AIPA/2002 amended 102(e) if appropriate (or pre-AIPA rules for PCT refs filed before Nov.29,2000); (3) consider benefit claims to earlier-filed provisionals/nonprovisionals only if subject matter is properly supported; (4) a provisional reference must have at least one claim supported by the provisional under pre-AIA 112 first paragraph; (5) PCT pubs not in English/did not designate US do not qualify for 102(e) and should be applied under 102(a)/(b); (6) use appropriate additional form paragraphs for double patenting, priority, and obviousness (e.g., 8.33–8.39, 7.13.fti, 7.14.fti, 7.21.01.fti). Must be preceded by 7.12.fti or 7.12.01.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.15.03.fti — Rejection under 102(e) where no common assignee or inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection that claims are anticipated under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) by a patent or patent application publication with an earlier filing date, where the reference is not required to have a common assignee or common inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply amended 102(e) as appropriate (AIPA/2002), consider whether the reference qualifies under 7.12.fti (PCT conditions, provisional support, benefit claims). If the reference is a PCT publication filed prior to Nov.29,2000 or not in English/did not designate US, do not use 7.15.03.fti — instead consider 102(a)/(b). Precede with 7.12.fti or other required paragraphs.
